exercises.question: Rarely _____ such dedication from a new employee during their first month on the job.
exercises.explanation: When negative or restrictive adverbs (rarely, seldom, never) are placed at the beginning of a sentence for emphasis, subject-auxiliary inversion is required.

exercises.question: Choose the correct inverted sentence.

options.A: Rarely I have seen such a beautiful view.
options.B: Rarely have I seen such a beautiful view.
options.C: Rarely I saw such a beautiful view.
options.D: Rarely did I have seen such a beautiful view.

exercises.correct_option: Rarely have I seen such a beautiful view.
exercises.explanation: After a negative/limiting adverb at the beginning, invert auxiliary and subject: Rarely have I seen.
